name: Ina Drew

summary.text: Ina Drew was Chief Investment Officer of JPMorgan Chase, heading the Chief Investment Office whose Synthetic Credit Portfolio lost more than $6 billion in 2012. She testified as a former CIO at the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations' March 15, 2013 hearing on the trades, and press coverage of the subcommittee's report said it singled her out, with former CFO Doug Braunstein, for particular criticism.

openQuestions: Site description of Drew as 'Chief Investment Officer who supervised the speculative credit trading strategy': supported as to her title and office; the word 'speculative' is the site's characterisation, though the subcommittee did find the portfolio was used for high-risk trading rather than hedging.
Drew's departure date from JPMorgan and any compensation clawback were not confirmed in this session (search budget exhausted).
